arxiv-1709-05455.title: Relative Kähler-Einstein metric on Kähler varieties of positive Kodaira dimension MSC 2010: 32Q15,32Q25, 32Q20
arxiv-1709-05455.creator: Hassan Jolany
arxiv-1709-05455.description: Abstract For projective varieties with definite first Chern class we have one type of canonical metric which is called Kähler-Einstein metric. But for varieties with an intermidiate Kodaira dimension we can have several different types of canonical metrics. In this paper we introduce a new notion of canonical metric for varieties with an intermidiate Kodaira dimension.

arxiv-1803-02653.title: On the Expressiveness and Monitoring of Metric Temporal Logic
arxiv-1803-02653.creator: Hsi-Ming Ho \rsuper a, Joël Ouaknine \rsuper b, James Worrell \rsuper a
arxiv-1803-02653.description: Abstract . It is known that Metric Temporal Logic ( MTL ) is strictly less expressive than the Monadic First-Order Logic of Order and Metric ( FO[ < , + 1 <,+1 ] ) when interpreted over timed words; this remains true even when the time domain is bounded a priori .

arxiv-1812-03249.title: Measuring scientific buzz
arxiv-1812-03249.creator: Kishore Vasan, Jevin West
arxiv-1812-03249.description: Abstract Keywords are important for information retrieval. They are used to classify and sort papers. However, these terms can also be used to study trends within and across fields. We want to explore the lifecycle of new keywords. How often do new terms come into existence and how long till they fade out?

arxiv-2107-12362.title: Pressure Test: Quantifying the impact of positive stress on companies from online employee reviews
arxiv-2107-12362.creator: Sanja Šćepanović, Marios Constantinides, Daniele Quercia, Seunghyun Kim
arxiv-2107-12362.description: Abstract Workplace stress is often considered to be negative, yet lab studies on individuals suggest that not all stress is bad. There are two types of stress: distress refers to harmful stimuli, while eustress refers to healthy, euphoric stimuli that create a sense of fulfillment and achievement.

arxiv-2203-09400.title: Analysis of quantum correlations within the ground state of a three level Lipkin model
arxiv-2203-09400.creator: Javier Faba, Vicente Martín, Luis Robledo
arxiv-2203-09400.description: Abstract The performance of beyond mean field methods in solving the quantum many body problem for fermions is usually characterized by the correlation energy measured with respect to the underlying mean field value. In this paper we address the issue of characterizing the amount of correlations associated to different approximations from a quantum information perspective.

arxiv-2311-08674.title: High-Precision Fruit Localization Using Active Laser-Camera Scanning: Robust Laser Line Extraction for 2D-3D Transformation
arxiv-2311-08674.creator: Pengyu Chu, Zhaojian Li, Kaixiang Zhang, Kyle Lammers, Renfu Lu
arxiv-2311-08674.description: Abstract Recent advancements in deep learning-based approaches have led to remarkable progress in fruit detection, enabling robust fruit identification in complex environments. However, much less progress has been made on fruit 3D localization, which is equally crucial for robotic harvesting.

arxiv-2408-14591.title: Bursts of star formation and radiation-driven outflows produce efficient LyC leakage from dense compact star clusters SLUG ( da Silva et al. 2012 ; Krumholz et al. 2015 ) , PETSc ( Balay et al. 1997 ; Balay et al. 2021 ) , NumPy ( Harris et al. 2020 ) , SciPy ( Virtanen et al. 2020 ) , Matplotlib (
arxiv-2408-14591.creator: Shyam H. Menon, Blakesley Burkhart, Rachel S. Somerville, Todd A. Thompson, Amiel Sternberg
arxiv-2408-14591.description: Abstract The escape of LyC photons emitted by massive stars from the dense interstellar medium of galaxies is one of the most significant bottlenecks for cosmological reionization. The escape fraction shows significant scatter between galaxies, and anisotropic, spatial variation within them, motivating further study of the underlying physical factors responsible for these trends.

arxiv-2507-17048.title: Dopant-induced stabilization of three-dimensional charge order in cuprates
arxiv-2507-17048.creator: Zheting Jin, Sohrab Ismail-Beigi
arxiv-2507-17048.description: Abstract We investigate the microscopic mechanisms behind the stabilization of three-dimensional (3D) charge order by Pr doping in YBa 2 Cu 3 O 7 (YBCO7). Density-functional-theory calculations locate the lowest-energy Pr superlattices for both Ba- and Y-site substitution. In the Ba-site case, the smaller Pr ion pulls the surrounding atoms inward.

arxiv-2507-18427.title: Strong time regularity and decay of 𝐋 ∞ \mathbf{L}^{\infty} solutions to 2 × 2 2\times 2 systems of conservation laws
arxiv-2507-18427.creator: Luca Talamini
arxiv-2507-18427.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Luca Talamini. We consider 𝐋 ∞ \mathbf{L}^{\infty} solutions to 2 × 2 2\times 2 systems of conservation laws. For genuinely nonlinear systems we prove that finite entropy solutions (in particular entropy solutions, if a uniformly convex entropy exists) belong to C 0 ​ ( ℝ + , 𝐋 l ​ o ​ c 1 ​ ( ℝ ) ) C^{0}(\mathbb{R}^{+};\mathbf{L}^{1}_{loc}(\mathbb{R})) . Our second result establishes a dispersive-type decay estimate for vanishing viscosity solutions. Both results are unified by the use of a kinetic formulation.

arxiv-2507-21081.title: Empathy in Explanation
arxiv-2507-21081.creator: Katherine M. Collins kmc61@cam.ac.uk, Kartik Chandra kach@mit.edu, Adrian Weller aw665@cam.ac.uk, Jonathan Ragan-Kelley jrk@mit.edu, Joshua B. Tenenbaum jbt@mit.edu
arxiv-2507-21081.description: Abstract Why do we give the explanations we do? Recent work has suggested that we should think of explanation as a kind of cooperative social interaction, between a why-question-asker and an explainer. Here, we apply this perspective to consider the role that emotion plays in this social interaction.

plos-pone-0005203.creator: David A. Hanauer, Daniel R. Rhodes, Arul M. Chinnaiyan
plos-pone-0005203.description: PLOS ONE research article. The vast amounts of clinical data collected in electronic health records (EHR) is analogous to the data explosion from the “-omics” revolution. In the EHR clinicians often maintain patient-specific problem summary lists which are used to provide a concise overview of significant

plos-pone-0350129.creator: Zhenmei Song, Wenli Li, Jie Zeng, Xuexin Wang, Dezhi Wang, Xingchen Liao

pmc-10521479.title: The “home-based exercise for breast and prostate cancer patients during treatment—a feasibility trial” (BENEFIT CA trial): rationale and methodological protocol
pmc-10521479.creator: Larissa Xavier Neves da Silva, Jayne Santos Leite, Andresa Conrado Ignacio, Fernanda Dias Massierer, Lucinéia Orsolin Pfeifer, Linda Ariene dos Santos Cardoso, Tainá Silveira Alano, Daniel Umpierre
pmc-10521479.description: BackgroundPhysical activity has been shown to benefit patients undergoing adjuvant cancer therapy. Although exercise interventions may be applied in several settings, most trials have focused on specialized facilities for their interventions. While these approaches benefit the access for individuals living near exercise centers, it hampers the assessment of real-world effectiveness.

pmc-10632874.title: Risk factors associated with progression from papilloedema to optic atrophy: results from a cohort of 113 patients
pmc-10632874.creator: Ruben Attia, Ruben Fitoussi, Kevin Mairot, Sarah Demortiere, Jan-Patrick Stellman, Penelope Tilsley, Bertrand Audoin, Thierry David, Natacha Stolowy
pmc-10632874.description: BackgroundThe aim of this study was to assess the risk factors for atrophic progression of patients with papilloedema secondary to intracranial hypertension, using optical coherence tomography parameters.MethodsA retrospective study was conducted at Marseille University Hospitals’ Ophthalmology departments between December 2015 and December 2021. All patients with papilloedema resulting from elevated intracranial hypertension at the initial presentation were included.

pmc-11313374.title: Photoinactivation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Mycobacterium smegmatis by Near-Infrared Radiation Using a Trehalose-Conjugated Heptamethine Cyanine
pmc-11313374.creator: Nataliya V. Kozobkova, Michael P. Samtsov, Anatol P. Lugovski, Nikita V. Bel’ko, Dmitri S. Tarasov, Arseny S. Kaprelyants, Alexander P. Savitsky, Margarita O. Shleeva
pmc-11313374.description: The spread of multidrug-resistant mycobacterium strains requires the development of new approaches to combat diseases caused by these pathogens. For that, photodynamic inactivation (PDI) is a promising approach. In this study, a tricarbocyanine (TCC) is used for the first time as a near-infrared (740 nm) activatable PDI photosensitizer to kill mycobacteria with deep light penetration.

pmc-11354634.title: Integrative Analysis of Transcriptomic Profiles and Physiological Responses Provide New Insights into Drought Stress Tolerance in Oil Palm (Elaeis guineensis Jacq.)
pmc-11354634.creator: Fernan Santiago Mejía-Alvarado, Arley Fernando Caicedo-Zambrano, David Botero-Rozo, Leonardo Araque, Cristihian Jarri Bayona-Rodríguez, Seyed Mehdi Jazayeri, Carmenza Montoya, Iván Ayala-Díaz, Rodrigo Ruiz-Romero, Hernán Mauricio Romero, Hunseung Kang
pmc-11354634.description: Oil palm (Elaeis guineensis Jacq.) is a highly productive crop economically significant for food, cosmetics, and biofuels. Abiotic stresses such as low water availability, salt accumulation, and high temperatures severely impact oil palm growth, physiology, and yield by restricting water flux among soil, plants, and the environment.

pmc-11386233.title: Arterial stiffness in adults with Long COVID in sub‐Saharan Africa
pmc-11386233.creator: Chikopela Theresa, Bwalya Katebe, Cyndya A. Shibao, Annet Kirabo
pmc-11386233.description: Severe acute coronavirus‐2 (SARS‐CoV‐2) infection has been associated with endothelial damage, and impaired nitric oxide production, which results in arterial stiffness and increased risk of cardiovascular disease. Long COVID is a term used to describe the persistence or the development of new symptoms that can occur after an acute infection.

pmc-11453546.title: 7407 Normosmic Idiopathic Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism in Women: A Case Report and Comprehensive Review
pmc-11453546.creator: E G Bustamante, M Sulehri, I Patoli, A Karunakaran
pmc-11453546.description: Disclosure: E.G. Bustamante: None. M. Sulehri: None. I. Patoli: None. A. Karunakaran: None. Introduction: IHH is a rare genetic disorder affecting gonadotropic-releasing hormone (GnRH) production and/or action, resulting in diminished sex steroid levels. Characterized by the absence of spontaneous pubertal development. In women, it manifests with normal adrenarche but absent thelarche and menarche.

pmc-11463079.title: Cardiometabolic risk in children and adolescents with obesity: a position paper of the Italian Society for Pediatric Endocrinology and Diabetology
pmc-11463079.creator: Giuliana Valerio, Procolo Di Bonito, Valeria Calcaterra, Valentino Cherubini, Domenico Corica, Luisa De Sanctis, Anna Di Sessa, Maria Felicia Faienza, Elena Fornari, Lorenzo Iughetti, Maria Rosaria Licenziati, Melania Manco, Emanuele Miraglia del Giudice, Anita Morandi, Mariacarolina Salerno, Maria
pmc-11463079.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Despite the implementation of preventive measures to counteract the obesity epidemics, the prevalence of childhood obesity is still alarming all over the world. Childhood obesity is the most common risk factor for both cardiovascular and metabolic diseases. In fact, an earlier onset of obesity can cause a greater risk of adiposity tracking across the lifespan and consequently a longer exposure to cardiometabolic risk factors.

pmc-12529855.title: Exploration of the GRAS family in Dimocarpus longan: identification, characterization, expression analysis and DlGRAS24 role in flowering time
pmc-12529855.creator: Jiasui Cao, Xuelian Sang, Liqin Liu, Jinlin Gou, Yao Liu, Ci Ren, Zhixin Zhang, Dengwei Jue, Shengyou Shi
pmc-12529855.description: BackgroundLongan is a perennial woody plant, and flowering is crucial for its development and the improvement of its economic value. The GRAS gene family has an important impact on how plants respond to both biotic and abiotic stressors as well as their growth and development. However, current research on the GRAS gene family in longan remains relatively limited.

pmc-12539102.title: Correlates of mild behavioural impairment in older adults: a scoping review
pmc-12539102.creator: Bada Kang, Seolah Yoon, Innhee Jeong, Dahye Hong, Jennifer Ivy Kim
pmc-12539102.description: BackgroundMild behavioural impairment in older adults has emerged as a potential precursor to cognitive decline and the onset of dementia. While the characteristics of mild behavioural impairment are documented, less is known about its correlates. A clearer understanding of these correlates could improve early detection and intervention strategies.

pmc-12570242.title: Veterans regaining control; preliminary effects of inpatient Dialectical Behavior Therapy based PTSD treatment
pmc-12570242.creator: Gerda Wesseling, Evelyn Nispeling, Juernene Tholel, Shanna Teunissen, Kathleen Thomaes
pmc-12570242.description: Introduction: Trauma-focused therapy (TFT) is highly effective in posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). However, there is some evidence that TFT is less effective in specific groups, such as veterans and people with comorbid personality disorders, emotion regulation problems or substance use disorders.

pmc-12575933.title: Exploring the safety and immunogenicity of the VLA15 vaccine among healthy or high-risk population: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-12575933.creator: Tayyaba Naseem Abbasi, Muhammad Saad Khan, Erum Siddiqui, Muhammad Ahmed Zaheer, Areeba Tabassum, Naila Zainab, Aminath Waafira
pmc-12575933.description: Background:Lyme disease, the most common vector-borne illness in the Northern Hemisphere, is caused by Borrelia burgdorferi and transmitted via tick bites. With rising global incidence and no approved human vaccine, VLA15, a novel recombinant vaccine targeting six OspA serotypes, shows promise as an effective preventive strategy.

pmc-12592691.title: Acupuncture's Multisystem Neuroimmunomodulation: Central–Peripheral Interactions in Gastroenteric, Psychiatric, and Chronic Pain Disorders
pmc-12592691.creator: Lijuan Zhang, Yucai Luo, Ting Wei, Dan Wang, Zhaoxuan He, Lei Lan, Fang Zeng
pmc-12592691.description: BackgroundAcupuncture, an ancient therapeutic modality rooted in traditional Chinese medicine, has evolved into a globally recognized intervention. Mounting evidence indicates that modulation of central–peripheral interactions constitutes a key pathophysiological mechanism underlying its efficacy. This review examines how acupuncture bridges neural, immune, and endocrine systems through these dynamic interactions to address complex modern diseases.

pmc-12996000.title: RS-WaterQuality Mapper: an open-source water quality remote sensing toolbox in QGIS
pmc-12996000.creator: Haibin Su, Hongxing Liu, Lei Wang, Ekaterina Miliutina, Jilin Men, Dan Tian, Yuehan Lu, Song Shu, Richard Beck, Amanjit Premsagar
pmc-12996000.description: Effective water management requires frequent monitoring, but traditional methods are limited in spatiotemporal scope. While satellite remote sensing provides extensive data, a gap persists in accessible, integrated software for non-specialists. To address this, we developed the RS-WaterQuality Mapper, an open-source Python plugin for QGIS.

pmc-13231025.title: Comparative Analysis of Dental Treatment Accuracy Using 2.5× Magnification Loupes Versus the Naked Eye: A Randomized Clinical Trial
pmc-13231025.creator: Talacheeru Rohit, Sravya Sri Prudhvi, Sreenivas Nagarakanti, Sandhya B, Hareesh Bandi, Kunapareddy Madhu Hasini
pmc-13231025.description: BackgroundMagnification systems such as dental loupes have been increasingly incorporated into clinical dental practice to improve visualization, precision, and ergonomics. However, evidence evaluating their effectiveness during routine periodontal procedures performed by dental interns remains limited. The present study aimed to assess the effect of 2.5× dental magnification loupes on psychomotor skill acquisition and clinical treatment outcomes during ultrasonic scaling.

pmc-13317295.title: The LEF1–LAG3 axis regulates CD4+ T cell function during Plasmodium yoelii NSM infection
pmc-13317295.creator: Wenbo Peng, Guikuan Liang, Keyu Lu, Feng Mo, Xiongyu Xie, Mingjie Chen, Haiwen Yuan, Lixin Luo, Xingyue Wang, Long Xu, Haixia Wei, Lu Li, Shan Zhao, Hongyan Xie, Xingfei Pan, Jun Huang
pmc-13317295.description: BackgroundCD4⁺ T cells are pivotal in coordinating anti-malarial immunity, while co-inhibitory receptors such as LAG3 critically regulate their function. However, the phenotype of LAG3⁺CD4⁺ T cells during Plasmodium infection and the upstream molecular mechanisms regulating LAG3 expression remain incompletely elucidated.MethodsWe established a murine model using Plasmodium yoelii NSM (P. yoelii NSM).

pmc-13421822.title: Comparing reported and observed use of insecticide-treated nets in Tanganyika, Democratic Republic of the Congo: a post-campaign longitudinal household study
pmc-13421822.creator: Nono Mvuama, Josue Zanga, Osée Y Sanogo, Baudouin Matela, Tiffany Clark, Aklilu Seyoum, Kristin Banek, Emery Metelo, Victoire Nsabatien, Eric Mafuta, Aimée Lulebo, Yung-Ting Bonnenfant, Michael Humes, Ferdinand Ntoya, Sheila Ogoma Barasa, Paul Mansiangi, Romain Jouffroy, Fiacre Agossa, Seth Irish
pmc-13421822.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAccurate measurement of insecticide-treated net (ITN) use is essential for evaluating malaria control programs. Most routine indicators rely on self-reported ITN use, which may be affected by recall and social desirability biases.

pmc-13452583.title: Experimental evidence for early bacterial inheritance in the giant kelp, Macrocystis pyrifera
pmc-13452583.creator: Sara Usandizaga, Jessica Beltrán, Gustavo Rodríguez-Valdecantos, Génesis Parada-Pozo, Marie-Laure Guillemin, Sylvain Faugeron, Nicole Trefault, Carolina Camus, Julie Olson
pmc-13452583.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Bacteria associated with macroalgae influence the development, health, and ecological interactions of their hosts. Although vertical transmission of bacterial symbionts has been proposed in some algal species, evidence remains limited. In this study, we combined 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to assess bacterial presence and localization throughout early developmental stages of the brown macroalga Macrocystis pyrifera.

pmc-13578607.title: Socioeconomic Determinants Associated With Overweight and Obesity in Adults in Southern Tehran: A Cross‐Sectional Study
pmc-13578607.creator: Shahla Arameshiyan, Masud Yunesian, Alireza Oliyaimanesh, Najmeh Almolouk Amini, Mahnaz Ashoorkhani
pmc-13578607.description: Background and AimsOverweight and obesity represent major public health challenges shaped by social, economic, behavioral, and environmental determinants. This study aimed to identify socioeconomic factors associated with overweight and obesity among adults living in southern Tehran in order to inform targeted, context‐specific prevention strategies.

pmc-13603819.title: A Removable 3D-Printed Protective Cap for Chronic Cranial Implants in Rhesus Macaques (Macaca mulatta): A Descriptive Case Series and Technical Refinement
pmc-13603819.creator: Rochelle D. Moore, Dorsa Amirkhany, Kelsey Clark, Behrad Noudoost
pmc-13603819.description: Simple SummaryBrain research in Rhesus macaques often requires surgically implanted devices, such as headposts and recording chambers, to measure brain activity over long periods. Monkeys naturally scratch and groom around these implants, which can damage the skin, delay healing, increase the risk of infection, and sometimes require additional surgeries or early removal from research studies.

pmc-7618841.title: Gut Healthism: The Penetrating Gaze and Depoliticising Forces of Direct-to-Consumer Microbiome Testing Kits
pmc-7618841.creator: Erica Zurawski, Maya Hey
pmc-7618841.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In recent years, scientific attention towards the gut has interpellated everyday consumers to test and intervene on their gut microbiome in the hopes of improving their overall health. Based on a discursive analysis of direct-to-consumer testing kits, we detail how their rhetoric individualises health interventions in the name of procuring a ‘healthy’ gut microbiome while obscuring the social, communal and environmentally predicated relations that inhere to a kind of health reliant on microbes.
